gaps.sentence: He was elected ___ chairman of the board.
gaps.explanation: No article is used with unique roles after 'elect', 'appoint', 'become'.

gaps.sentence: They sailed across ___ Mediterranean last summer.
gaps.explanation: Seas and oceans take 'the': the Mediterranean.

gaps.sentence: ___ number of applicants has doubled this year.
gaps.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('has'); 'a number of' would take 'have'.

gaps.sentence: He was offered ___ job in the human resources department.
gaps.explanation: 'A job' — first mention of one of many possible jobs. Note: 'in human resources' takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ honest answer would have saved everyone time.
___ Dutch consistently rank among the best non-native English speakers.
gaps.explanation: 'The + nationality adjective' refers to the people of that country as a group.
